title: A bundle still has loose ends
hook: Which layout removes the depicted free-end paths?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: Bundling the middle leaves ends that can still weave through loops. The drawing distinguishes keeping strands together from restricting the ends’ routes.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.
objective: Bundling the middle leaves ends that can still weave through loops. The drawing distinguishes keeping strands together from restricting the ends’ routes.

claims.text: Bundling the middle leaves ends that can still weave through loops. The drawing distinguishes keeping strands together from restricting the ends’ routes.
claims.source: W-383 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): retyped from source (Raymer & Smith 2007, p.16435, which could not be opened from this host) to derivation, as FC LH-2 asked. Argument: if both ends of a cord are held, the cord is a fixed arc and no motion of its middle can change its knot type, so a new knot needs a free end to pass through a loop. A tie around the middle leaves every end free; ties that also secure the ends leave none. On the stage this is the drawing: one middle tie and 2N orange end dots, against ties at both ends and the middle with 0 end dots, for N=2..8 (src/lib/lifehacks/home-models.ts evaluateHome, homeCordScene). Earlier history: FC LH-2 held it unverified only because its sole source was unopenable.

claims.text: Plain cord; storage only. The drawing gives no electrical safety limit or product-specific bend radius.
claims.source: Scope limits and illustrative assumptions of this card; Free ends=2×cord count before,0 depicted accessible ends after securing; knots/tangles not simulated. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: caption "Plain cord; storage only" and reveal limit present; drawing is strands, ties and end dots only.

claims.text: Free ends=2×cord count before,0 depicted accessible ends after securing; knots/tangles not simulated.

claims.text: Which layout removes the depicted free-end paths?
claims.source: Chosen comparison question; the prediction refers to the stated default values and selected methods. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: rendered question; key = 1 "Secure bundle ends", the only layout with 0 drawn ends.

claims.text: Bundling the middle keeps the strands together but leaves the ends free, and free ends weaving through loops are the tangle path. Securing the ends removes that path in the drawing.

recall.question: You put one tie around the middle of a coiled cord and leave both ends hanging. How can it still tangle with its neighbours?
options: The tie makes the cord stiffer
Its free ends can weave through loops
Nothing can tangle once the middle is tied tight
recall.why: Bundling the middle keeps the strands together but leaves the ends free, and free ends weaving through loops are the tangle path. Securing the ends removes that path in the drawing.
